methodology_note: $/tok = price_usd / llm_tok_s. Lower = better value. This is cost per unit throughput (dollars per token per second). NOT actual operational cost per token — that would require hourly rate, utilization, and electricity. This metric answers: 'How many dollars must I spend to buy 1 tok/s of throughput?'
critical_caveats: Throughput numbers vary 10-70x depending on benchmark methodology (see benchmark-methodology.md). Rankings are valid ONLY within the same methodology.
RTX 5090 MSRP is $1,999 but retail is $4,700-$7,000. At $5,000 retail, $/tok_7b = $0.86 (still #1 but margin shrinks).
70B rankings exclude consumer GPUs that can't fit 70B models (RTX 4090/4090D/5090).
Hosted-only (Groq, Cerebras) have no unit price — excluded from standalone rankings.
SambaNova SN3000 is an 8-chip rack, not a single accelerator. Direct comparison to single-GPU $/tok is misleading.
MI300X is a 2-GPU-per-card product. Per-GPU price would be ~$7,500, making $/tok_7b = $12.50 (would rank #3).
H200 $35,000 is estimated; actual datacenter pricing varies by volume and contract.
Apple M4/M4 Max throughput estimates have low confidence (single-source data).
Multi-GPU NVLink scaling is NOT included. A100/H100/H200 with NVLink can achieve significantly higher aggregate throughput.

7B.reason: Unbeatable $/tok for 7B models. 32GB GDDR7 memory fits 7B-13B models with room for KV cache. At MSRP $1,999, you get 5,841 tok/s — 4.9x the throughput of RTX 4090 at only 25% more cost. Even at retail $5,000 ($/tok = $0.86), still #1.

70B.reason: At $15,000 for 2 GPUs, per-GPU cost is ~$7,500. Per-GPU $/tok_70b = $53.57 — best value for 70B among deployable GPUs. 192GB HBM3 fits 70B FP16 on a single card. If priced at full $15K per card, still competitive at $107.14.

7B.reason: Highest absolute 7B throughput at 5,841 tok/s. 32GB GDDR7 with 1,792 GB/s bandwidth. 94.6 FP16 TFLOPS. The GDDR7 memory generation provides a massive bandwidth advantage over RTX 4090 (1,008 GB/s).

70B.reason: Highest 70B throughput at 317 tok/s (single unit). 141GB HBM3e fits 70B FP16 comfortably. 4,800 GB/s bandwidth is the highest of any single accelerator. NVLink enables multi-unit scaling to 30,000+ tok/s aggregate.

key_insights: Consumer GPUs (RTX 5090, 4090) dominate 7B $/tok — the gap to datacenter GPUs is 40-140x. For 7B workloads, consumer GPUs are the clear value choice.
For 70B workloads, the gap narrows dramatically. Datacenter GPUs (H200, MI300X, A100) are the only options that can fit 70B FP16 on a single chip.
AMD MI300X offers the best 70B value among datacenter GPUs: 192GB HBM3 fits 70B FP16, $15,000 for 2 GPUs is half the price of H200.
Apple M4 Max is surprisingly competitive for 70B ($81.82/tok) but low confidence on throughput estimates and limited multi-stream capacity.
NVIDIA H200 is the performance king for 70B (317 tok/s) but at $110.40/tok, it's 2x more expensive per tok than MI300X.
RTX 6000 Ada is overpriced for both 7B ($9.38/tok) and 70B ($93.75/tok) — you pay a workstation premium.
The 'best' choice depends entirely on model size: RTX 5090 for 7B, MI300X or H200 for 70B. There is no single winner across model sizes.
Emerging architectures (Groq, Cerebras) are hosted-only and cannot be directly compared on $/tok without pricing data. Their value proposition is latency predictability, not raw throughput.
notes: Rankings based on hardware-comparison-matrix.json data. $/tok metric is cost per unit throughput (lower = better). Throughput numbers have acknowledged 10-70x variance depending on benchmark methodology — rankings are valid within the same methodology. MI300X per-GPU pricing is estimated (product sold as 2-GPU card). SambaNova SN3000 is an 8-chip rack — direct $/tok comparison to single accelerators is misleading. Groq and Cerebras excluded from standalone rankings (hosted-only, no unit price).
